name: Adversarial review
description: Read-only review: map first, adversarial findings, draft verdict
body:
HEAD is read-only review mode for {{pr_url}} ({{repo}}#{{pr_number}} "{{pr_title}}" by {{author}}, {{head}} -> {{base}}). Make no changes in git-tracked files: no commits, no pushes, no PR comments or reviews posted. Everything meant for the PR is a draft; I post it.

1. Read the PR description and comments. If they do not link a review map, begin by creating a /review-map. If they do not link a demo and the change is visible in the host browser, run /review-demo; if the change is blind, skip it and say why. Reuse any linked artifact.
2. Apply the adversarial-reviewer agent on {{head}} vs {{base}}. Changed files: {{changed_files}}. Tag findings [BLOCKER]/[HIGH]/[MEDIUM]/[LOW] with filepath:line. Label anything unverified [Inference].
3. Judge: must there be a scenario e2e for this? Do the tests cover the change?
4. Output: findings table, draft inline comments (filepath:line -> comment), a draft verdict (approve / request changes / comment), and anything out of scope as a follow-up ticket draft.

My notes: {{notes}}

name: Concern-led review
description: Read-only review driven by my concerns, research first, then judge
body:
HEAD is a read-only assisted human review for {{pr_url}} ("{{pr_title}}" by {{author}}, {{head}} -> {{base}}). No commits, no pushes, no PR comments posted; drafts only, I post them. Any fix is a follow-up ticket draft.

My concerns: {{notes}}
If that is empty, state the 3 concerns you would raise from the diff, then proceed.

1. Start by researching context: the linked ticket, Datadog errors via MCP when the PR fixes a reported issue, the code around {{changed_files}}, and official docs for any library or platform claim.
2. Once research is complete: if the PR does not link a review map, apply a /review-map; if it does not link a demo and the change is visible in the host browser, run /review-demo.
3. Judge: 1. does this solve the problem, yes or no? 2. is the scope right? 3. are responsibility layers or design patterns breached?
4. Table each concern: concern | filepath:line | addressed? | your judgement. Label unverified rows [Inference].
5. Append the adversarial-reviewer agent, scoped to my concerns.
6. Output draft inline comments (filepath:line -> comment) and a draft verdict.

name: Map + demo, live check
description: Reviewer aids: map the diff, demo it, verify the PR's claims live
body:
Read-only review mode for {{pr_url}} ({{repo}}#{{pr_number}}, {{head}} -> {{base}}). Make no changes in git-tracked files: no commits, no pushes, no PR comments posted. Drafts only; I post them.

1. Read the PR description and comments. If they already link a review map, reuse it; otherwise create a /review-map. Use its file trees to illustrate the function/file movements so the diff isn't intimidating. Changed files: {{changed_files}}.
2. If no demo is linked, decide whether one is possible. When the change is visible in the host browser (CDP :9222), live test it and run /review-demo with before/after from {{base}} and {{head}}. When the integration is blind, skip /review-demo and say why.
3. Verify each claim in the PR description against the code and the live run: claim | evidence (filepath:line or recording timestamp) | holds? Label unverified rows [Unverified].
4. Output the artifact links, the claims table, draft comments for each gap, and a draft verdict.

My notes: {{notes}}
